_about: T1199 review (2026-11-27): the owner's calls on EDGE WATER the closure-area cutter leaves open — a boundary river drawn wiggling across a reserve's or park's edge, every crossing a graze under 5 m, which the cutter does not count as a crossing, although the owner's rule is that edge water stays closed. The builder does not decide it (AGENTS rule 12): the area-cut gate's G6 stops the atlas build and names every such stretch (area, blue line, measure range) no accepted row covers. Key: area (area id), blk + water (the blue line and its name), from_m / to_m (the stretch, route measures; never a section id). call `closed`: the stretch is edge water of that area, the cutter treats it as inside (it joins the member run); call `open`: it stays open, accepted. Every row has a note. Only `accepted` rows are read, each with accepted_by + accepted_on; `proposed` rows are Claude's proposals for the owner and are read by nothing (a proposal is no acceptance). An accepted row that matches no stretch any more is stale and stops the build too. Authored by the owner by hand; read by pipeline.atlas.splits.area_edge_calls (the closure cutter in build.cut_closure_areas, and area_cut_gate G6); checked by check_curated --waters.

accepted.note: Beaverfoot River along Yoho: 123 m within the band, 2 grazes of up to 0.3 m. G6 of the area-cut gate (T1199 review round 2, 2026-11-27): an open stretch lying within the 50 m edge band for more than the 100 m floor with two grazes into the polygon, both under the 5 m dip, so the cutter leaves it open. Opened by the graze fix (before it, the graze counted as a crossing and the band closed it). Picture: lane E pictures/T1199-edge-two-lines.png. OWNER 2026-11-27 (T1199, relayed verbatim by the planning chat): "Merge with the list; close both edge stretches (Recommended)" — closed as edge water.
